newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: GDP drop seen depressing S.Africa shares next week.
newsitem.headline: GDP drop seen depressing S.Africa shares next week.

text.p: South African shares are seen flat to weak next week with recently-reported negative first quarter gross domestic product (GDP) growth failing to inspire hopes for an interest rate cut, portfolio analysts and dealers said on Friday.

An unexpected drop in GDP, which fell 0.8 percent, boosted the market on Thursday with fleeting expectations that a cut could come sooner rather than later, but the market fell on Friday as the hopes quickly faded.

"I do not think (Reserve Bank governor Chris) Stals will be convinced to cut rates yet. He will wait until the relaxation of foreign exchange controls. Our fundamentals have not changed," a portfolio manager who declined to be identified said.

The market saw a rash of economic indicators this week, with consumer price inflation, money supply and credit extension providing some much-needed directon after several weeks of aimless drifting. But the direction could be down.
Dealers cited disappointing company results as a negative factor. The latest was South African Breweries Ltd last week with year earnings per share rising 12 percent to 633.7 from 566.2 last year.
Portfolio managers said unless results improved or rates were cut, the market would remain under pressure.

"If we continue to have results like SAB then the market will remain weak. We need an interest rate cut or companies to report decently. Otherwise the market is right to be at these weak levels," Greg Amoils, a portfolio manager at Irish Menell Rosenberg, told Reuters.
Johan Marais, director at Societe General Frankel Pollack, said the market would remain under pressure for the next few weeks.
"We see the market going slowly down. No panic selling or anything. Obviously there will be a bounce here and there. But the market will be slowly driven down over the next couple of weeks," he said.

Gold shares were seen remaining weak with a slight rally -- inspired by soaring platinum prices -- failing to impress the market. Dealers said the rally was not related to bullion fundamentals and therefore players doubted its sustainability.
There are no major economic indicators due next week and the market will look to Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd and Sappi Ltd results for direction.
Anglo was seen harvesting wealthy year earnings up by about 27 percent profits from its sister companies De Beers Consolidated Mines Ltd and Minorco SA.

Analysts polled by Reuters forecast a consensus headline earnings per share figure of 2,220.5 cents compared to the previous year's 1,743 cents. Their numbers lay within a range of 2,165 and 2,294 cents.
But pulp and paper producer Sappi Ltd was seen posting a miserable set of first half results next week as the firm continued to be hamstrung by a hostile price environment.
